what: NOT the T0.5 measurement. A workstation CPU run that exercises the instrument and demonstrates its inconclusive branch. The real number is KGPU, on 2x T4 with -ngl 99.
host: local workstation, 16 vCPU, CPU-only (--ngl 0 --threads 8), other work running concurrently
finding: The tool correctly refused this measurement. total_ratio 0.968 says full capture is FASTER than no callback at all, which cannot be true; the run-to-run spread is 25.9%, larger than the effect. Reporting 0.968 would have fed a fabricated speedup into the Phase 5 projection and from there into Gate Q1, which decides whether the study collects 1M or 500k tokens per model.
implication: The real T0.5 run needs a quiet machine and enough repeats that the spread is well under the effect. A Kaggle session is quieter than this workstation, but the guard stays either way.

side_evidence.determinism: All five streams byte-identical across the 4 independent full-capture processes, so T3.4's CPU half still holds after the --capture-mode change.
side_evidence.reshard_invariance: The single 12-doc run's topk.bin and logits.bin are byte-identical to the concatenation of runC's three 4-doc shards produced by the pre-change binary. tokens.bin differs only in the FLAG_HIDDEN_CAPTURED bits, because runC ran --hidden-stride 1 and this run used the default 20; token_id, doc_id and pos_in_doc are identical. The refactor is data-preserving and resharding-invariant.
